Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-64d1c0a1","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 15.1 Scope of MSL's Indemnity","rationale":"Section 15.1 gives us a vendor-side indemnity from MSL covering (a) third-party IP infringement (patent, trademark, trade name, copyright, mask work, trade secret) arising from MSL's performance, procured Parts, processes, designs, deliverables or pre-existing materials, (b) MSL's failure to comply with law, and (c) failure to perform its warranty/support obligations — the core of the preferred position. Exclusions are the usual ones (IBM-selected marks, IBM written specifications, IBM-provided defective designs), and Section 15.2 supplies standard procedure (prompt notice, cooperation, MSL control with our right to participate at our expense) plus procure/redesign remedies at MSL's expense. There is no reciprocal IBM indemnity of MSL anywhere in the Agreement, and Appendix A §5 adds a further MSL indemnity for Microsoft code, so the allocation runs in our favour. Minor points noted but not flagged: the indemnity names IBM rather than IBM and its affiliates, and does not separately call out data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; also, the mutual 3%-of-bill-of-materials cap in Section 15.3(b) would on its face apply to indemnity recoveries — that cap is properly addressed under the limitation-of-liability rule rather than double-flagged here.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-9b27a24a","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 13.0 INTELLECTUAL AND INDUSTRIAL PROPERTY","rationale":"The Agreement meets the preferred position and runs in our favour throughout. Section 13.1 (p0197) has MSL assign to IBM all intellectual and industrial property rights in the hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products delivered, and p0198 extends IBM ownership (with MSL assignment) to any invention MSL makes on Products or on IBM processes and systems, with MSL only retaining a use right for performing its obligations here — i.e. deliverables and work product vest in us with no joint ownership. Section 13.3(a) (p0208) expressly protects our pre-existing IP: nothing grants MSL any rights or licences in IBM's pre-existing IP except a royalty-free licence to use IBM confidential information under the AECI solely to manufacture Products for IBM, with any further licence requiring a separate signed agreement. Confidential information disclosed to MSL is returnable on demand (13.2(c)), and under the Loan Agreement Section 5 (p1530) IBM retains title to all Loaned Items with no transfer rights for MSL. On tooling, SOW 21.1(e) (p1105) confirms all tools, dies, jigs, patterns, equipment or Parts purchased, furnished, charged to or paid for by IBM become and remain IBM property; MSL's ownership of generic \"Common Tooling\" (p1088) is precisely the vendor-tools carve-out the playbook accepts. No provision assigns IBM IP, data or classified parts information to MSL, and there is no joint ownership. Two minor sub-elements worth noting but not flagging: there is no express licence-back of MSL background IP embedded in Products (mitigated by the breadth of the 13.1 assignment plus the bar on MSL using proprietary assembly/test processes), and there is no standalone \"Customer Data\" ownership sentence, which is unsurprising in a 1998 manufacturing outsourcing deal where information flows are governed by the AECI.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-b5380163","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 15.3 Limitations of Liability","rationale":"Section 15.3 contains a mutual cap and a mutual consequential-damages waiver, but the cap basis fails the fallback: 3% of the bill-of-materials value of all Products delivered over the entire term is far below twelve months' (or even six months') fees, so MSL's exposure is effectively illusory relative to the volume it manufactures for us. The cap is also expressed as covering \"total liability ... regardless of the form of action, whether contract or tort,\" with no carve-outs, so MSL's indemnities under Section 15.1 (third-party IP infringement, regulatory non-compliance, warranty support) and its confidentiality obligations sit inside this very low cap with no super-cap — the walk-away scenario in the rule. We therefore reset the basis to the greater of twelve months' amounts paid or payable and USD 1,000,000 and added a single carve-out sentence for indemnification, confidentiality/data security, IP infringement, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud, plus confirmation that our payment obligations are not capped damages. Mutuality is preserved, so the edit does not disturb the existing bargain beyond the cap basis and carve-outs.","proposal":"Reset the mutual cap to the greater of 12 months' amounts paid/payable and USD 1,000,000, and place indemnities, confidentiality, IP infringement, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IBM's payment obligations outside the cap.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-44452088","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 16.2 Assignment","rationale":"§ 16.2 imposes a blanket consent requirement on IBM's assignments with no affiliate or M&A/successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard on MSL's consent, which is walk-away territory under this rule (the only reasonableness qualifier runs in MSL's favour for MSL Related Company assignments). It therefore fails even the fallback (mutual right to assign to successors on written notice). We redlined the first sentence to add the affiliate/successor carve-out for IBM plus a not-unreasonably-withheld standard, leaving MSL's assignments consent-gated. No change-of-control provisions exist anywhere in the document, so MSL has no termination or re-pricing right on an IBM change of control (§ 16.5 addresses only MSL's own sale or merger and requires the successor to assume performance), which is consistent with the preferred position.","proposal":"Add IBM affiliate/successor assignment carve-out and a reasonableness standard in § 16.2.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-c0fde954","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 6.0 PURCHASE OF PRODUCTS","rationale":"This meets the preferred position: nothing binds IBM to buy exclusively or to source solely from MSL. Scope of Work (§3.0) covers only \"selected manufacturing, Integration, and other Services\", and the SOW purchase clause (§6.0) is a generic purchase commitment driven by Purchase Orders, with no \"exclusive\", \"sole supplier\", \"all of its requirements\" or \"shall not procure from any third party\" language anywhere in the Base Agreement, SOW, or attachments. The agreement in fact assumes IBM's freedom to move volume elsewhere — §9.0(e) expressly contemplates \"reductions of Products requirements due to migration to a competitive supplier\". The only sole-source style restrictions run against MSL (e.g. IBM Nominated Suppliers, Prohibited Suppliers at §16.15, and IBM Parts used solely in IBM Products), which benefit us and are not flagged. Any volume/forecast commitments are addressed under MINCOMMIT rather than double-flagged here.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-b87da691","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 6.1 Cancellation of Purchase Order","rationale":"The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty or minimum-fee obligation payable by IBM as customer, which meets the preferred position. A full-text search for \"liquidated\" returns nothing, and the only \"penalty\" mechanic (§7.3 b), p0757 — responsiveness shortfall penalty applied to MSL's Work Center material cost and invoiced by IBM to MSL) runs in our favour, as do the delinquency-based Shipment Profit Rate adjustments and §10.4 (MSL bears premium costs of late shipment). Termination provisions impose no exit fee on IBM: §6.1 lets IBM cancel Purchase Orders at any time with no cancellation charge, and §§5.2–5.3 limit IBM to paying for completed/partially completed Product and Parts actually procured against IBM forecasts — cost reimbursement rather than a stipulated penalty. On inventory risk, §13.2 e) expressly states IBM \"will have no liability for unused flexibility\" and §13.3 b) leaves untransferred EOL inventory as MSL's sole responsibility. Nothing to redline.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-055a780e","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 13.3 Licenses","rationale":"Every licence grant in this agreement runs from us (IBM) to the counterparty (MSL), not the reverse: §13.3(a) gives MSL only a narrow royalty-free right to use IBM confidential information to manufacture Products solely for IBM; §24.1(a) and the Equipment and Program Loan Agreement §§5-6 likewise grant MSL limited, use-restricted rights in IBM software, Loaned Programs and Licensed Internal Code. Those restrictions benefit our side and are not flagged. Our own position is stronger than the preferred licence position rather than weaker: under §13.1 IBM \"assumes and will assume ownership and MSL assigns and will assign all intellectual and industrial property rights for hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products\", plus assignment of MSL inventions on Products and on IBM processes, and MSL is barred from using proprietary processes for the Products absent written agreement — so we hold ownership rather than a revocable licence, and there is no grant to us that MSL can revoke at will or that excludes our affiliates or contractors. Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording but are noted only: the agreement contains no IBM affiliate/\"Related Company\" extension (the concept is used only for MSL) and no express licence-back of MSL background IP for transition to a replacement manufacturer; successor/assignment mechanics sit in §16.2 and §16.5 (with MSL warranting that any acquirer assumes performance) and are addressed under the assignment rule rather than double-flagged here.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-2ed0ec5c","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 14.18 Restrictions and Limitations","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no non-compete, field-of-use, territory or exclusivity restriction on IBM, so it meets the preferred position (no restriction on Customer). The restriction-flavoured provisions all run the other way and are therefore acceptable: § 14.18 limits MSL's use of IBM property and MSL's competing Integration activity, and § 16.15 (Prohibited Suppliers) constrains MSL's sourcing. §§ 3.0 and 11.0 are scope-of-work only and contain no requirements/sole-source commitment obliging IBM to buy exclusively from MSL, so our freedom to build in-house or dual-source is unimpaired. The confidentiality carve-out at p1490–1491 affirmatively preserves each Recipient's right to provide products or services competitive with the Discloser's and to supply the Discloser's competitors, which benefits us. § 5.1(v) is a change-of-control termination trigger rather than a covenant. Noted but not flagged under this rule: § 9.0(f) binds IBM not to solicit Transferred Employees for a stated period, but that is a personnel non-solicit (time-limited, with inbound-applicant and general-advertising carve-outs), not a restriction on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build; it belongs to any non-solicitation rule rather than this one. No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-dd6667e0","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 4.0 TERM","rationale":"The Agreement runs for a committed three-year initial term (Section 4.0; mirrored in SOW Section 2.0) and Section 5.0 permits termination only \"for cause\" — material breach, insolvency events, change of control or force majeure (Section 5.1 a)–c)). There is no right for IBM to terminate for convenience at any point during the multi-year term; the only no-cause exit is a six-month (twelve-month under the SOW) non-renewal notice that bites only at the end of a term. That fails both the preferred position (30 days' notice) and the fallback (60–90 days' notice with a capped early-termination fee), and sits in walk-away territory (\"no Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term\"). The PO-level cancellation right in SOW Section 6.1 lets us cancel individual Purchase Orders but does not give an agreement-level exit and is expressly subject to cost reimbursements, so it does not cure the gap. On the other side of the ledger the position is acceptable: MSL likewise has no mid-term convenience right and any non-renewal requires at least six months' notice, so no vendor-side redline is needed. We have therefore added a new Section 5.4 giving IBM a 30-day convenience right with a refund of prepayments, while preserving MSL's payment entitlements under Sections 5.2 and 5.3 and confirming MSL has no reciprocal mid-term convenience right.","proposal":"Add an IBM termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' notice, with refund of prepayments and no MSL mid-term convenience right","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-2e8d0070","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 7.0 AUDIT","rationale":"Every audit, inspection and verification right in the Agreement runs in our favour: Section 7.0 (process audits at MSL facilities), Section 13.1 (audit/inspect consigned Products), Section 21.3 (tooling inspection), Section 24.1 (IBM retains the right to audit), Attachment 6 Section 4.0 and Appendix A Section 4 (IBM/MS audits of MSL's books, records and facilities on 45 days' notice, at IBM's cost unless material discrepancies are found). Section 16.14 imposes only a mutual record-retention obligation and grants no audit right. Searches for reciprocal MSL rights to audit or inspect IBM's records, usage or systems returned nothing, so no audit right binds us as Customer and there is no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access exposure to constrain. Nothing to redline — flagging the IBM-side audit rights would remove a protection we benefit from.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-ee1daa03","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 16.9 Governing Law","rationale":"Section 16.9 selects New York substantive law and requires any action to be commenced \"in a court sited within the State of New York\" — courts, not arbitration. No arbitration provision appears anywhere in the document, and the ancillary general clauses (CI Agreement Section 8, p1499, and Loan Agreement Section 16, p1587) also choose New York law, so there is no conflicting law or venue selection. This meets the preferred position (New York law with New York courts). Minor points short of the preferred wording, noted only: venue is not expressly the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, and the clause adds a contractual limitations period; neither is material and neither is redlined.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-68505699","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"ATTACHMENT 1","rationale":"The sole most-favoured-nation provision in the Agreement runs in IBM's favour: MSL undertakes to price its engineering services to IBM on a \"most favored customer\" basis (Attachment 1, p1099). Searches for MFN triggers (\"most favored\", \"no less favorable\", \"best price\", \"favorable\", \"match\", third-party terms) and a review of the pricing provisions (§§ 7.1, 7.2, and the Markup Appendix) reveal no obligation on IBM to extend MSL any terms given to third parties or to match third-party offers. This meets the preferred position (no MFN burden on the customer, vendor-granted MFN welcome), so no redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-1290ea35","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 6.0 PURCHASE OF PRODUCTS","rationale":"There is no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment on us. § 6.0 obliges us to purchase only Products we order (\"This Agreement does not authorize MSL to produce or deliver any Product\"), and § 6.1 lets us cancel any and all Purchase Orders at any time, so fees follow ordered volumes only — the preferred position. Our residual volume-related exposure is expressly limited: § 13.2(e) states \"IBM will have no liability for unused flexibility\"; § 13.3(b) leaves EOL inventory not transferred as MSL's sole responsibility; and § 13.0(f) confirms we have no liability for inventory MSL purchases so long as forecast accuracy meets the Appendix 2 level. The only payment obligation tied to volumes is the Appendix 2 requirements-accuracy compensation (a defined percentage of material cost payable if our forecast accuracy falls below the stated threshold), which operates as a forecast true-up compensating MSL for material it bought against our forecast rather than a shortfall penalty or multi-year take-or-pay; it is quantified, quarterly and self-liquidating. Noted for the record but not a deviation: the true-up has no aggregate cap, which we would only pursue if reopening the pricing appendices.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-df47ee96","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 9.0 PERSONNEL","rationale":"Section 9.0(f) is the only hiring restriction in the Agreement (16.7 and 5.2 contain no personnel-hiring constraints), and it binds IBM. It sits at the playbook fallback on all material terms: (i) scope is narrow — limited to the finite, listed group of \"Transferred Employees\" (the ex-IBM staff who moved to MSL to perform the work), not all MSL personnel; (ii) it is a solicitation-only restriction with no \"no-hire\" — IBM may in fact hire Transferred Employees who approach it or respond to advertising; and (iii) both required carve-outs are present, for unsolicited approaches on the individual's own initiative and for general employment advertising/communications and independent search firms. Two points short of the preferred position are noted rather than flagged: the covenant is one-way rather than mutual, and the duration is redacted (\"[*] years\") and runs from the Effective Date rather than from the end of an individual's involvement. We should confirm on the unredacted copy that the period does not exceed 24 months (walk-away); as drafted from a fixed Effective Date rather than a rolling engagement date, the restriction is self-limiting and does not warrant a redline.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-c8662efe","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 4.0 TERM","rationale":"Both term clauses auto-renew with non-renewal notice windows far beyond the fallback ceiling of 60 days: the Base Agreement § 4.0 requires six months (~180 days) notice, and SOW Attachment § 2.0 requires twelve months (~365 days) notice against a mere six-month renewal period, meaning notice must be given before the renewal even begins. Windows longer than 90 days are walk-away territory under the rule, so this fails the fallback on a material term. Redline shortens both windows to 30 days and aligns renewal periods at 12 months (preferred position); a 60-day window remains an acceptable fallback. The vendor reminder and price-uplift cap are absent, but renewals continue on the same terms and conditions, so uplift risk is limited and we note this rather than press it.","proposal":"Shorten non-renewal notice to 30 days and fix renewal terms at 12 months in both Base Agreement § 4.0 and SOW Attachment § 2.0","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-transition-ea7e556f","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 5.2 Rights Upon Termination","rationale":"Exit protection exists and runs in our favour. Section 5.2(a)(ii) obliges MSL to \"assist in the transfer of MSL responsibilities and Products as described in Attachment 1: Statement Of Work, to IBM or to another party that IBM designates\" on expiry or termination for default, with no cap on the assistance window (better for us than the 6-month/90-day benchmarks), and 5.2(a)(iii) requires return of all IBM documentation and all discs, tapes and media containing IBM confidential information within a defined period after termination. Attachment 6 Section 3(a) adds return of master media plus signed written certification of compliance, and Section 13.2(c) lets IBM demand immediate return of confidential information at any time during the term. Nothing permits MSL to withhold or immediately destroy IBM data, so there is no walk-away exposure. Minor points noted only: the return period in 5.2(a)(iii) is redacted so we cannot confirm it is 30 days or less, deletion-and-certification is expressed only for the Attachment 6 MS Software Images rather than all IBM data, and there is no express machine-readable format requirement. These are sub-elements short of the preferred wording and do not warrant a redline.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-warranty-26130e7e","ruleId":"WARRANTY","ruleTitle":"Performance warranty and duration","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 19.1 Scope of Warranty","rationale":"MSL gives a real express warranty in our favour: SOW § 19.1 warrants conformance in all material respects to IBM specifications plus specified quality, good workmanship and freedom from defect, with stated periods for MSL Procured Parts (19.1(a)(iv)) and workmanship (19.1(a)(v)), running from delivery, surviving acceptance testing and expressly covering latent defects (19.1(b)). The remedy set matches the playbook: § 19.5 requires failure analysis, repair or replacement within the stated turnaround at MSL's expense and, if repair or replacement is not possible, a refund of MSL's price for the failed Product and Parts; § 19.7 adds epidemic-failure recall cost coverage, which exceeds the preferred position. The § 19.6 disclaimer is confined to implied and other terms relating to quality, merchantability, conformance and fitness and expressly preserves \"MSL'S WARRANTY OBLIGATIONS DESCRIBED IN THIS SECTION 19\", so it does not swallow the express warranty; there is no \"AS IS\" language. Two points noted but not flagged: (i) the durations in 19.1(a)(iv)-(v) are redacted ([*] months), so we should confirm on execution that they are at least 12 months for Products/Parts, and (ii) § 16.19 sunsets all representations and warranties on the [*] anniversary of the Effective Date, which we should confirm does not cut short Product warranties on units delivered late in the term. This is a manufacturing/Products deal, so the absence of a separate professional-and-workmanlike services warranty, compliance-with-laws warranty and malicious-code warranty is immaterial here, and the warranty exclusions in 19.1(a)(ii)-(iii) relate to IBM Parts and consigned Products (our own materials) and 19.3 to misuse, both customary. The clause benefits us, so no redline.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-insurance-bbc202ba","ruleId":"INSURANCE","ruleTitle":"Vendor insurance","severity":"low","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 13.1 Consigned Products","rationale":"The Agreement contains no vendor insurance covenant. The only insurance references are narrow and property-specific: SOW 13.1(b) requires MSL to carry replacement-value cover for IBM consigned Products (with IBM as joint insured); SOW 21.2 obliges IBM (not MSL) to insure IBM-owned tooling; Loan Agreement Section 8 relieves MSL of risk of loss on Loaned Items; and 10.0 defers premises terms to a separate Lease of Premises Agreement not before us. **From:** In-house counsel 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Outsourcing Agreement, Statement of Work and ancillary agreements

On balance the document is favourable to us: intellectual property, indemnification, audit, warranty, exit assistance and pricing protections all run in our direction, and there is no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-purchase or liquidated-damages burden on us.

- **Vendor insurance (low, missing).** No general liability, professional liability, cyber or workers' compensation covenant, despite MSL occupying our premises, holding our consigned inventory and accessing our networks and customer integration data.

---

## 2. Findings

| 7 | High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 6.1 Cancellation of Purchase Order |
| 8 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.3 Licenses |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 14.18 Restrictions and Limitations |
| 10 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | **Deviation** | § 4.0 Term (and SOW Attachment § 2.0) |
| 11 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 7.0 Audit |
| 12 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 16.9 Governing Law |
| 13 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | Attachment 1 |

### 3.1 Limitation of liability — § 15.3 (critical)

**Proposal.** Reset the mutual cap to the greater of twelve months' amounts paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, and place indemnities, confidentiality/data security, IP infringement, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and our payment obligations outside the cap. Mutuality is preserved, so the edit does not disturb the existing bargain beyond the cap basis and carve-outs.

### 3.2 Termination for convenience — § 4.0 / § 5.0 (high)

The Agreement runs for a committed three-year initial term (§ 4.0, mirrored in SOW § 2.0) and § 5.0 permits termination only for cause — material breach, insolvency, change of control or force majeure (§ 5.1(a)–(c)). There is no right for us to terminate for convenience during the term; the only no-cause exit is a non-renewal notice that bites at the end of a term. The PO-level cancellation right in SOW § 6.1 lets us cancel individual Purchase Orders but does not provide an agreement-level exit and is subject to cost reimbursement. MSL likewise has no mid-term convenience right, so no vendor-side reciprocity issue arises.

**Proposal.** Add a new § 5.4 giving us a convenience right on 30 days' notice with refund of prepayments, preserving MSL's payment entitlements under §§ 5.2 and 5.3 and confirming MSL has no reciprocal mid-term convenience right.

### 3.3 Assignment — § 16.2 (high)

This fails even the fallback (mutual right to assign to successors on written notice). Separately, there are no change-of-control provisions binding us — § 16.5 addresses only MSL's own sale or merger and requires the successor to assume performance — which is consistent with our preferred position.

**Proposal.** Amend the first sentence of § 16.2 to add an affiliate/successor assignment carve-out for us plus a not-unreasonably-withheld standard, leaving MSL's assignments consent-gated.

### 3.4 Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice — § 4.0 and SOW Attachment § 2.0 (medium)

Both term clauses auto-renew with non-renewal notice windows well beyond our 60-day fallback ceiling: § 4.0 requires six months' notice, and SOW Attachment § 2.0 requires twelve months' notice against a six-month renewal period — meaning notice must be given before the renewal period even begins.

**Proposal.** Shorten both windows to 30 days and align renewal periods at twelve months; a 60-day window remains acceptable as a fallback. Renewals continue on the same terms and conditions, so we are not pressing for a price-uplift cap or vendor reminder mechanic.

### 3.5 Vendor insurance — missing (low)

This matters because MSL occupies our premises, holds our and our customers' consigned inventory, and accesses our applications, networks and customer integration data under SOW § 24.1.

**Proposal.** Insert a new § 16.22 in the General section at preferred limits (CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request), expressly preserving the existing consigned-Products cover. Fallback limits (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) can be offered in the covering comment.

---

## 4. Walk-away items

Two findings fall into walk-away territory under our playbook and should not be conceded without escalation:

1. **§ 15.3 — cap with no carve-outs.** A 3%-of-bill-of-materials cap applying to MSL's IP indemnity and confidentiality obligations, with no super-cap, is the express walk-away scenario under LOL-CAP. We need, at minimum, carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality/data security, IP infringement, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud, and confirmation that our payment obligations are not capped damages.
2. **§ 4.0 / § 5.0 — no convenience exit in a multi-year term.** "No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term" is walk-away under T4C. A 60–90 day notice period with a capped early-termination fee is our fallback landing zone.

The six- and twelve-month non-renewal windows in § 4.0 and SOW § 2.0 also exceed the 90-day walk-away threshold under RENEWAL, though we regard this as negotiable to the 30–60 day range rather than escalation-worthy in isolation.

---

## 5. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the four deviations and the new insurance section: § 15.3 (cap basis and carve-outs), new § 5.4 (convenience termination), § 16.2 (affiliate/successor carve-out and reasonableness), § 4.0 and SOW Attachment § 2.0 (notice windows and renewal periods), and new § 16.22 (insurance). Comments to carry the `[Playbook]` prefix with fallbacks stated where noted above.
2. **Escalate the two walk-away items** (§ 15.3 and the absence of a convenience right) to the business sponsor before the next negotiation session, so we know our authority on the cap basis and any early-termination fee.
3. **Obtain the unredacted execution copy** and confirm three redacted figures: the non-solicit period in § 9.0(f) (walk-away above 24 months), the warranty durations in § 19.1(a)(iv)–(v) (we want at least twelve months for Products and Parts), and the confidential-information return period in § 5.2(a)(iii) (we prefer 30 days or less).
4. **Confirm the interaction of § 16.19** (sunset of representations and warranties on a stated anniversary of the Effective Date) with Product warranties on units delivered late in the term, so warranty cover is not cut short.
5. **Request the Lease of Premises Agreement** referenced at SOW § 10.0, which was not provided and may bear on premises-related insurance and risk allocation.
6. **Note for the record, not for redline:** the absence of an aggregate cap on the Appendix 2 forecast-accuracy true-up. We would pursue this only if the pricing appendices are reopened for other reasons.

No other provisions require amendment. The IP, indemnity, audit, warranty, exit-assistance, governing law, MFN, exclusivity, non-compete, licence-grant and minimum-commitment positions are compliant and, in several cases, better than our preferred position; we should resist any counterparty attempt to reopen them."}
